clock_unit: original finite monotonic seconds, same gateway boot/controller
predicates: started_mono is sampled once where the existing deadline is derived, before connection; deadline=started+original reserve seconds, never reset.
request_started_mono is the original actual pre-conn.request sample after current authority/admission.
read_completed_mono is sampled at actual successful read1 EOF/framing checks, before capture/fsync/SQLite finalization.
Original phase_start <= started <= request_started <= read_completed < deadline; deadline-started <=120 and original phase/whole deadline bounds hold.
Missing pre-send/read observations remain null on failure; no successful transport proof may contain them.

Header arrays preserve exact original get_all values and duplicates. Refuse >1 CL/TE/CE/CT, CL together with TE, invalid/non-ASCII/nondecimal/oversize CL, TE other than chunked ignoring case and surrounding whitespace, or CE other than absent/exact identity.
Content type agrees with original outer capture, using original application/octet-stream default only when absent.
Content-Length equals exact original response byte count and remaining_length=0.
Chunked transfer requires original chunked=true, response_closed=true and remaining_length null or0.
Close-delimited response requires no CL/TE, chunked=false, remaining_length=null, response_closed=true and actual EOF.
eof_observed=true only when original read1 returns empty before deadline; a watchdog shutdown at/after deadline refuses.
Original raw response hash/length, completion, explicit incomplete and streaming terminal-event predicates remain mandatory. HTTP EOF alone is insufficient.
Original failed/incomplete/cancelled dispatches retain unknown liability and cannot qualify preparation; no refunds.
compatibility: New cohort capture extension; old legacy ledger/close rows and existing Settlement two-field transport contract remain unchanged.
Original historical captures without these facts remain insufficient for this new transport predicate; no reconstructed EOF/time/header fields.
No extra provider sends, no enlarged allocations, and no actual execution authorized.
